name: Superalloys & Refractory Metals
summary: Studies the nickel-base superalloys and refractory metals that make jet engines and rocket engines possible at temperatures near their melting points.

topics.name: Requirements of gas-turbine and rocket-engine hot sections
Ni-base superalloy metallurgy: gamma matrix and gamma-prime precipitates
Strengthening mechanisms: order strengthening, anomalous yield, solid-solution and carbides
Topologically close-packed phases and alloy design (PHACOMP, d-electron methods)
Wrought, cast, directionally solidified and single-crystal superalloys
Investment casting of single-crystal turbine blades; grain selectors and defects
Oxidation-resistant coatings: aluminides, MCrAlY bond coats and thermal barrier coatings
Refractory metals: Nb, Mo, Ta, W and Re; their alloys and oxidation problem
Niobium alloys (C-103) for rocket nozzle extensions
Superalloys for oxygen-rich rocket engines and hydrogen environments
Emerging high-temperature alloys: refractory high-entropy alloys, Mo-Si-B, silicides
